edits.original: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam until Moshe, even over those whose sins weren't like Adam's disobedience, who is a foreshadowing of the one who was to come.
edits.final: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam until Moshe, even over those whose wrongdoings weren't like Adam's disobedience, who is a foreshadowing of the one who was to come.
notes: Precise contextual construction: whose sins weren't like Adam's disobedience → whose wrongdoings weren't like Adam's disobedience

edits.original: The gift is not as through one who sinned: for the judgment came by one to condemnation, but the free gift came of many trespasses to justification.
edits.final: The gift is not as through one who acted wrongly: for the judgment came by one to condemnation, but the free gift came of many trespasses to justification.
notes: Precise contextual construction: one who sinned → one who acted wrongly

edits.original: For as through the disobedience of one person many were made sinners, even so through the obedience of the one, many will be made righteous.
edits.final: For as through the disobedience of one person many came to be marked by moral failure, even so through the obedience of the one, many will be made righteous.
notes: Precise contextual construction: many were made sinners → many came to be marked by moral failure

edits.original: The law came in besides, that the trespass might abound; but where sin abounded, grace abounded more exceedingly;
edits.final: The law came in besides, that the trespass might abound; but where wrongdoing abounded, grace abounded more exceedingly;
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: that as sin reigned in death, even so grace might reign through righteousness to life of the age through Yeshua the Messiah, our Master.
edits.final: that as wrongdoing reigned in death, even so grace might reign through righteousness to life of the age through Yeshua the Messiah, our Master.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: May it never be! We who died to sin, how could we live in it any longer?
edits.final: May it never be! We who died to wrongdoing, how could we live in it any longer?
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: knowing this, that our old self was crucified with him, that the body of sin might be done away with, so that we would no longer be in bondage to sin.
edits.final: knowing this, that our old self was crucified with him, that the body of wrongdoing might be done away with, so that we would no longer be in bondage to wrongdoing.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: For the one who has died has been freed from sin.
edits.final: For the one who has died has been freed from wrongdoing.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: For the death that he died, he died to sin one time; but the life that he lives, he lives to God.
edits.final: For the death that he died, he died to wrongdoing one time; but the life that he lives, he lives to God.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: Thus consider yourselves also to be dead to sin, but alive to God in Messiah Yeshua our Master.
edits.final: Thus consider yourselves also to be dead to wrongdoing, but alive to God in Messiah Yeshua our Master.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: Neither present your members to sin as instruments of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God, as alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness to God.
edits.final: Neither present your members to wrongdoing as instruments of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God, as alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness to God.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: For sin will not have dominion over you. For you are not under law, but under grace.
edits.final: For wrongdoing will not have dominion over you. For you are not under law, but under grace.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: What then? Shall we sin, because we are not under law, but under grace? May it never be!
edits.final: What then? Shall we do wrong, because we are not under law, but under grace? May it never be!
notes: Precise contextual construction: Shall we sin → Shall we do wrong

edits.original: Don't you know that to whom you present yourselves as servants to obedience, his servants you are whom you obey; whether of sin to death, or of obedience to righteousness?
edits.final: Don't you know that to whom you present yourselves as servants to obedience, his servants you are whom you obey; whether of wrongdoing to death, or of obedience to righteousness?
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: But thanks be to God, that, whereas you were bondservants of sin, you became obedient from the heart to that form of teaching whereunto you were delivered.
edits.final: But thanks be to God, that, whereas you were bondservants of wrongdoing, you became obedient from the heart to that form of teaching whereunto you were delivered.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: Being made free from sin, you became bondservants of righteousness.
edits.final: Being made free from wrongdoing, you became bondservants of righteousness.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: For when you were servants of sin, you were free in regard to righteousness.
edits.final: For when you were servants of wrongdoing, you were free in regard to righteousness.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: But now, being made free from sin, and having become servants of God, you have your fruit of sanctification, and the result of life of the age.
edits.final: But now, being made free from wrongdoing, and having become servants of God, you have your fruit of sanctification, and the result of life of the age.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is life of the age in Messiah Yeshua our Master.
edits.final: For the wages of wrongdoing is death, but the free gift of God is life of the age in Messiah Yeshua our Master.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: For when we were in the flesh, the sinful passions which were through the law, worked in our members to bring forth fruit to death.
edits.final: For when we were in the flesh, the passions shaped by wrongdoing which were through the law, worked in our members to bring forth fruit to death.
notes: Precise contextual construction: sinful passions → passions shaped by wrongdoing

edits.original: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? May it never be! However, I wouldn't have known sin, except through the law. For I wouldn't have known coveting, unless the law had said, "You shall not covet."
edits.final: What shall we say then? Is the law wrongdoing? May it never be! However, I wouldn't have known wrongdoing, except through the law. For I wouldn't have known coveting, unless the law had said, "You shall not covet."
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: But sin, finding occasion through the commandment, produced in me all kinds of coveting. For apart from the law, sin is dead.
edits.final: But wrongdoing, finding occasion through the commandment, produced in me all kinds of coveting. For apart from the law, wrongdoing is dead.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: I was alive apart from the law once, but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died.
edits.final: I was alive apart from the law once, but when the commandment came, wrongdoing revived, and I died.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: for sin, finding occasion through the commandment, deceived me, and through it killed me.
edits.final: for wrongdoing, finding occasion through the commandment, deceived me, and through it killed me.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: Did then that which is good become death to me? May it never be! But sin, that it might be shown to be sin, by working death to me through that which is good; that through the commandment sin might become exceeding sinful.
edits.final: Did then that which is good become death to me? May it never be! Rather, wrongdoing brought death to me through what is good, so that wrongdoing might be exposed for what it is; through the commandment, its destructive character became unmistakable.
notes: Whole-verse editorial construction retains source grammatical argument and figures

edits.original: For we know that the law is spiritual, but I am fleshly, sold under sin.
edits.final: For we know that the law is spiritual, but I am fleshly, sold under wrongdoing.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: So now it is no more I that do it, but sin which dwells in me.
edits.final: So now it is no more I that do it, but wrongdoing which dwells in me.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: But if what I don't desire, that I do, it is no more I that do it, but sin which dwells in me.
edits.final: But if what I don't desire, that I do, it is no more I that do it, but wrongdoing which dwells in me.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: but I see a different law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity under the law of sin which is in my members.
edits.final: but I see a different law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity under the law of wrongdoing which is in my members.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: I thank God through Yeshua the Messiah, our Master! So then with the mind, I myself serve God's law, but with the flesh, the sin's law.
edits.final: I thank God through Yeshua the Messiah, our Master! So then with the mind, I myself serve God's law, but with the flesh, the law of wrongdoing.
notes: Precise contextual construction: the sin's law → the law of wrongdoing

edits.original: For the law of the Ruach of life in Messiah Yeshua made me free from the law of sin and of death.
edits.final: For the law of the Ruach of life in Messiah Yeshua made me free from the law of wrongdoing and of death.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: For what the law couldn't do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God did, sending God’s own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, God condemned sin in the flesh;
edits.final: For what the law couldn't do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God did, sending God’s own Son in the likeness of flesh marked by wrongdoing and for wrongdoing, God condemned wrongdoing in the flesh;
notes: Precise contextual construction: sinful flesh → flesh marked by wrongdoing
Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: If Messiah is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the spirit is alive because of righteousness.
edits.final: If Messiah is in you, the body is dead because of wrongdoing, but the spirit is alive because of righteousness.
notes: Personified hamartia and domination imagery in Romans 5–8

edits.original: This is my covenant to them, when I will take away their sins."
edits.final: This is my covenant to them, when I will take away their moral failures."
notes: Precise contextual construction: their sins → their moral failures

edits.original: I wrote to you in my letter to have no company with sexual sinners;
edits.final: I wrote to you in my letter to have no company with people engaging in sexual wrongdoing;
notes: Precise contextual construction: sexual sinners → people engaging in sexual wrongdoing

edits.original: yet not at all meaning with the sexual sinners of this world, or with the covetous and extortioners, or with idolaters; for then you would have to leave the world.
edits.final: yet not at all meaning with the people engaging in sexual wrongdoing of this world, or with the covetous and extortioners, or with idolaters; for then you would have to leave the world.
notes: Precise contextual construction: sexual sinners → people engaging in sexual wrongdoing

edits.original: But as it is, I wrote to you not to associate with anyone who is called a brother or sister who is a sexual sinner, or covetous, or an idolater, or a slanderer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner. Don't even eat with such a person.
edits.final: But as it is, I wrote to you not to associate with anyone who is called a brother or sister who is someone engaging in sexual wrongdoing, or covetous, or an idolater, or a slanderer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner. Don't even eat with such a person.
notes: Precise contextual construction: a sexual sinner → someone engaging in sexual wrongdoing

edits.original: Flee sexual immorality! "Every sin that a person does is outside the body," but the one who commits sexual immorality sins against their own body.
edits.final: Flee sexual immorality! "Every moral failure that a person commits is outside the body," but the one who commits sexual immorality does wrong against their own body.
notes: Precise contextual construction: Every sin that a person does → Every moral failure that a person commits
Precise contextual construction: sins against their own body → does wrong against their own body

edits.original: But if you marry, you have not sinned. If a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Yet such will have oppression in the flesh, and I want to spare you.
edits.final: But if you marry, you have not acted wrongly. If a virgin marries, she has not acted wrongly. Yet such will have oppression in the flesh, and I want to spare you.
notes: Precise contextual construction: you have not sinned → you have not acted wrongly
Precise contextual construction: she has not sinned → she has not acted wrongly

edits.original: But if any man thinks that he is behaving inappropriately toward his virgin, if she is past the flower of her age, and if need so requires, let him do what he desires. He doesn't sin. Let them marry.
edits.final: But if any man thinks that he is behaving inappropriately toward his virgin, if she is past the flower of her age, and if need so requires, let him do what he desires. He does no wrong. Let them marry.
notes: Precise contextual construction: He doesn't sin → He does no wrong

edits.original: Thus, sinning against the brothers and sisters, and wounding their conscience when it is weak, you sin against Messiah.
edits.final: Thus, wronging the brothers and sisters, and wounding their conscience when it is weak, you wrong Messiah.
notes: Precise contextual construction: sinning against the brothers and sisters → wronging the brothers and sisters
Precise contextual construction: you sin against Messiah → you wrong Messiah

edits.original: Wake up righteously, and don't sin, for some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.
edits.final: Wake up righteously, and do no wrong, for some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.
notes: Precise contextual construction: don't sin → do no wrong

edits.original: Or did I commit a sin in humbling myself that you might be exalted, because I preached to you God's good news free of charge?
edits.final: Or did I commit a moral failure in humbling myself that you might be exalted, because I preached to you God's good news free of charge?
notes: Precise contextual construction: commit a sin → commit a moral failure

edits.original: that again when I come my God would humble me before you, and I would mourn for many of those who have sinned before now, and not repented of the uncleanness and sexual immorality and lustfulness which they committed.
edits.final: that again when I come my God would humble me before you, and I would mourn for many of those who have acted wrongly before now, and not repented of the uncleanness and sexual immorality and lustfulness which they committed.
notes: Precise contextual construction: have sinned before now → have acted wrongly before now

edits.original: I have said beforehand, and I do say beforehand, as when I was present the second time, so now, being absent, I write to those who have sinned before now, and to all the rest, that, if I come again, I will not spare;
edits.final: I have said beforehand, and I do say beforehand, as when I was present the second time, so now, being absent, I write to those who have acted wrongly before now, and to all the rest, that, if I come again, I will not spare;
notes: Precise contextual construction: have sinned before now → have acted wrongly before now

edits.original: "We, being Judeans by nature, and not Gentile sinners,
edits.final: "We, being Judeans by nature, and not Gentiles considered wrongdoers,
notes: Precise contextual construction: Gentile sinners → Gentiles considered wrongdoers

edits.original: But if, while we sought to be justified in Messiah, we ourselves also were found sinners, is Messiah a servant of sin? Certainly not!
edits.final: But if, while we sought to be justified in Messiah, we ourselves also were found to have done wrong, is Messiah a servant of wrongdoing? Certainly not!
notes: Precise contextual construction: were found sinners → were found to have done wrong
Precise contextual construction: servant of sin → servant of wrongdoing
